title: Bounded decision-tree depth yields a narrow, tidy DNF
statement: Let $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2)$ — more precisely $f$ a Boolean function on $n$ variables — have decision-tree depth at most $d$. Then $f$ is computed by a DNF formula $\varphi$ (a disjunction of terms, each term a conjunction of literals) of width at most $d$, meaning every term of $\varphi$ contains at most $d$ literals, such that $\varphi(x) = f(x)$ for all inputs $x$. Moreover each term of $\varphi$ is tidy: no literal is repeated within a term, and no two literals in the same term share a variable (equivalently, within any one term each variable occurs at most once, and with a single fixed polarity).
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n variables
decision-tree depth of f is at most d
replaced:
If a Boolean function $f$ has decision-tree depth $\le d$, then there is a DNF $\varphi$
of width $\le d$ that computes $f$, with all terms nodup and variable-injective.
